ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of Figure A is an ideal transformer; the two ends of the primary coil are connected to an alternating voltage, and the right side of the secondary coil is connected to a load circuit containing L1, L2, R, L, D, and C; the question asks for the effective value of the voltage across the two ends of the secondary coil. Figure B is a sinusoidal curve of the voltage u across the two ends of the primary coil changing with time t, and the peak values marked by the dashed lines on the vertical axis are +36√2 V and -36√2 V. Then reason: the effective value of a sinusoidal alternating current is equal to the peak value divided by √2, so the effective value of the primary-coil voltage U1 = 36√2/√2 = 36 V. An ideal transformer satisfies U1:U2 = n1:n2 = 3:1, therefore U2 = U1/3 = 12 V. The external load connected to the secondary coil does not affect the voltage-ratio relationship of the ideal transformer.
